lessons.title: Nationalism and the road to independence and reunification
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level History — Nationalism, independence and reunification; constitutional history (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Explain what nationalism is and its causes
Describe the main steps to independence of French Cameroun and the future of the British Cameroons
Give the key dates of 1960 and 1961
reviewNotes: Historian to verify: UPC founding year (1948), 1 January 1960, 1 October 1960 (Nigeria), 11 February 1961, 1 October 1961, the two ballot options in the plebiscite, and the neutrality of the causes. Names of political leaders are deliberately omitted; the syllabus may require them.

Draft for historian review: only widely accepted facts and approximate dates are used; every date, name and interpretation must be verified by a history teacher before release. Political questions are stated neutrally.

blocks.md: **Nationalism** is a movement for self-government and national identity. After the Second World War, people across Africa and Asia called for independence. Causes in Cameroon included: the experience of foreign rule, taxes and forced labour, the example of other countries, the ideas of the United Nations Charter, the return of soldiers, and the growth of education and political parties, trade unions and associations.

blocks.caption: The road to independence and reunification

blocks.title: Steps in the French trust territory
blocks.md: Political parties and associations grew after the war; the **Union des Populations du Cameroun (UPC)** was founded in **1948** and called for independence and reunification. The administering power, the UN and political leaders discussed the future. **French Cameroun became independent on 1 January 1960.**

In the **British Cameroons**, political parties and associations also grew. **Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960**. The UN then decided that the people of the British Cameroons should vote in a **plebiscite** to choose between joining Nigeria or joining the independent Republic of Cameroon.

blocks.title: The plebiscite of 11 February 1961
blocks.md: The **Southern Cameroons** voted to join the **Republic of Cameroon**; the **Northern Cameroons** voted to join **Nigeria**. On **1 October 1961** the Southern Cameroons joined the Republic of Cameroon, forming the **Federal Republic of Cameroon** with two federated states: East Cameroon and West Cameroon.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- French Cameroun became independent in 1960, but the Southern Cameroons joined it in 1961; do not mix the dates.
- The plebiscite offered a choice between joining Nigeria or Cameroon; independence by itself was not on the ballot.
- Keep the account neutral: historians and citizens hold different views about events and arrangements; state the facts and the dates.

blocks.title: Example 1: dates
blocks.statement: Which events happened on 1 January 1960 and on 1 October 1961?
steps: On 1 January 1960 French Cameroun became independent.
On 1 October 1961 the Southern Cameroons joined the Republic of Cameroon.
Between them, on 11 February 1961, the plebiscite was held.
blocks.answer: Independence of French Cameroun (1960); reunification and the Federal Republic (1961).

blocks.title: Example 2: results
blocks.statement: How did the Northern and Southern Cameroons vote in the 1961 plebiscite?
steps: Southern Cameroons voted to join the Republic of Cameroon.
Northern Cameroons voted to join Nigeria.
Both results were accepted by the UN.

lessons.title: From the Federal Republic to the unitary state
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level History — Nationalism, independence and reunification; constitutional history (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Describe the structure of the Federal Republic of Cameroon (1961–1972)
State the date and nature of the 1972 referendum and the change to a unitary state
Outline later changes of name and constitution
Explain why bilingualism and national unity are stressed in the history of the state
reviewNotes: Historian to verify: 20 May 1972 referendum, 2 June 1972 proclamation of the United Republic, name change in 1984, constitution of 1996, structure of the federation, and that the account stays neutral on contested political questions. Teachers should add what the syllabus requires without opinion.

Draft for historian review: only widely accepted facts and approximate dates are used; every date, name and interpretation must be verified by a history teacher before release. Political questions are stated neutrally.

blocks.md: From **1 October 1961** the **Federal Republic of Cameroon** consisted of two federated states, **East Cameroon** (the former French Cameroun) and **West Cameroon** (the former Southern Cameroons), each with its own government and assembly, under a federal president and a federal government. English and French were the official languages.

blocks.title: The change in 1972
blocks.md: On **20 May 1972** a national referendum was held on a new constitution that replaced the federal structure with a **unitary state**. After the vote the country was named the **United Republic of Cameroon**, proclaimed on 2 June 1972. 20 May is celebrated as the **National Day**.

In **1984** the name of the country was changed to the **Republic of Cameroon**. A new constitution was adopted in **1996**; it defines Cameroon as a decentralised unitary state with two official languages and provides for regions and other institutions. The state continues to develop its institutions, and people hold different opinions on some questions of political organisation; in an exam, state the facts and the dates.

blocks.title: Symbols of unity
blocks.md: Cameroon is a bilingual country with English and French as official languages, a national flag, an anthem, a coat of arms and a motto. Many peoples and languages live together; national unity, peace and bilingualism are goals stated in public life and in education.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Do not confuse the two events: 1961 created the federation; 1972 ended it.
- Use the names correct for each period: Federal Republic (1961–1972), United Republic (1972–1984), Republic of Cameroon (1984 onwards).
- Do not take sides on political debates; give accurate dates and describe what each constitution says.

blocks.title: Example 1: name for each period
blocks.statement: What was the official name of the country in 1965, in 1975 and in 1990?
steps: 1965 falls in the federal period: Federal Republic of Cameroon.
1975 falls between 1972 and 1984: United Republic of Cameroon.
blocks.answer: Federal Republic; United Republic; Republic of Cameroon.

blocks.title: Example 2: federal and unitary
blocks.statement: Explain the difference between a federal and a unitary state.
steps: In a federal state powers are shared between a central government and state governments, each with its own institutions.
In a unitary state the central government holds the main power and divides the country into administrative units.
The 1972 change replaced the first model with the second.
blocks.answer: Federal: shared power between centre and states; unitary: central authority with administrative units.
